And I toldya two years ago Sora would have trouble commercializing.

@sama shoulda listened to me.


Gary Marcus (@GaryMarcus)

Standing by this prediction that Sora will see limited (not zero) professional use. 

Getting it to do exactly what you want, if you have specific expectations is going to be hard.



— https://nitter.net/GaryMarcus/status/1783916981554712876#m

Toldya Sora wasn’t getting us to AGI


Gary Marcus (@GaryMarcus)

Sora 2 is pretty clear evidence that ungodly amounts of compute still doesn’t yield AGI.



— https://nitter.net/GaryMarcus/status/1974840288360518084#m

Groups of agents don’t magically sort out the unreliability of individual agents. 

Instead, they often get stuck.


Rohan Paul (@rohanpaul_ai)

New research proves that current AI agent groups cannot reliably coordinate or agree on simple decisions.

Building teams of AI agents that can consistently agree on a final decision is surprisingly difficult for LLMs.

But problem is that developers frequently assume that if you have enough AI agents working together, they will eventually figure out ho

Terrifying AI twist on the Dunning-Kruger effect


Lukasz Olejnik (@lukOlejnik)

Does AI make us collectively dumber? Is "grok wat do u think" the new "I've outsourced my common sense to a chatbot and I feel great about it"? A study secretly made an AI give wrong answers half the time while people used it to solve logic puzzles. People followed the wrong AI 80% of the time. Their confidence went up regardless. This is the "cognitive surrender". The moment people stop asking "is this true?" and s

Nvidia has nearly doubled over the last two years. (12x over last five).

But it’s fallen since GPT-5 came out. 

People are no longer buying the hype.

The AI industry is spending big bucks to take down people who view them with skepticism.

One good example, likely first of many, is the tale of @AlexBores


Nancy Scola (@nancyscola)

I've got a new profile of Alex Bores—running for Congress in Manhattan and the prime target of the AI-industry-backed Super PAC Leading the Future—out today for @POLITICOMagazine. 

Some reporting nuggets…

Nonsense beats coherent prose every time.

Results are from GPT, but may perhaps be an apt metaphor for our time?


Christoph Heilig (@ChristophHeilig)

4/ The nonsense beats coherent prose in EVERY configuration. 18 out of 18. GPT-5, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4. With reasoning, without, maximum reasoning.
The nonsense wins every time.

Jensen is an absolute genius at guilting people into using his stuff—even if there is no demonstrable return on investment for them.


Gergely Orosz (@GergelyOrosz)

This whole segment just rubs me the wrong way

Jensen is very clearly talking up his book: wanting to see companies spend *much* more $$$ on GPUs / tokens... to increase NVIDIA revenue even more... to do the same thing as they already do (build software, as they have before)

An independent survey showed that 90%+ of my technical predictions are correct.  How is that not credible?

Calling on journalists to dismiss me is completely unprofessional.
